html:
"Minor states" is the map's label for the patchwork of small kingdoms in Anatolia and the Armenian highlands in 200 and 100 BCE. They filled the space between the big Hellenistic powers and Rome.

As the Seleucid Empire lost its grip on Anatolia, local dynasties, many of Persian descent, set up kingdoms of their own:

  • Bithynia in the northwest, on the Sea of Marmara.
  • Pontus on the Black Sea coast.
  • Cappadocia on the central plateau.
  • Galatia, where Celtic invaders settled in the 270s BCE.
  • Armenia and smaller realms such as Sophene and Commagene to the east.

Their courts mixed Greek culture with Persian and Anatolian traditions. Rome stepped in more and more. In the early 1st century BCE Mithridates VI of Pontus tried to unite the region against Rome, and Tigranes the Great briefly made Armenia an empire. Rome won the Mithridatic Wars, and by the 1st century CE most of these kingdoms were Roman provinces or clients.
sum: "Minor states" is the map's label for the patchwork of small kingdoms in Anatolia and the Armenian highlands in 200 and 100 BCE. They filled the space between the big Hellenistic powers and Rome.
